title: WhatConverts vs CallRail — Jon Martin

blocks.html: This comparison is for an agency or an in-house marketer deciding between WhatConverts and CallRail to attribute calls, and sometimes forms, to the campaigns behind them, with leads landing in HubSpot.
Both assign tracking numbers and record calls. They differ in what else they track, how they price, and how they reach HubSpot.

Choose WhatConverts if you need calls, forms, and chat in one report, or if you manage many client accounts. Choose CallRail if you want calls and texts to create HubSpot records directly, without building automations yourself.
Adding form tracking moves both tools up a tier, so price the tier you'll actually use, not the entry plan.

WhatConverts call tracking is $30 a month for a single account, plus usage, with $30 of usage credit included. Plus is $60 a month for a single account, plus usage; adds form and chat tracking. For agencies, Agency Plus is $500 a month for unlimited accounts, plus usage, with $250 of usage credit included. There's a 14-day free trial.

It tracks phone calls, forms, and chat, with the marketing source attached. Its HubSpot connection runs through Zapier workflows you set up yourself, so you need a Zapier account; once it's set up, new leads create HubSpot contacts, and deal values can flow back to WhatConverts.

CallRail's call tracking tier is $50 a month plus usage, with 5 numbers and 250 minutes included. The tier with forms is $95 a month plus usage; adds form tracking. Extra numbers are $3 each, and there's a 14-day free trial with no credit card.
CallRail creates HubSpot leads from inbound calls and texts, or adds activities to existing contacts, with recordings viewable in HubSpot. It serves the United States, Canada, the UK, and Australia.

sections.label: Fit for a small marketing team

blocks.html: If you run one brand and calls are the main lead source, CallRail's direct HubSpot integration is the simpler setup. If you run several brands or clients, WhatConverts' agency plan keeps them on one bill.
If forms and chat matter as much as calls, WhatConverts reports all three together on its Plus tier.
WhatConverts reaches HubSpot through Zapier, so someone has to build and maintain those workflows, and you pay for a Zapier account.
CallRail's form tracking costs a higher tier, and its service covers a short list of countries.
List your lead sources by volume. If calls dominate and you want the least setup, lean CallRail. If you need every channel in one report, lean WhatConverts.
Trial both on one campaign, then check that the source and campaign fields arrive in HubSpot the way your reports expect.
